PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies.

2. When learning Free-hand sketching, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Free-hand sketching.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Free-hand sketching.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Free-hand sketching.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Free-hand sketching.

3. When learning Safety in the Immediate Environment, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Safety in the Immediate Environment.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Safety in the Immediate Environment.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety in the Immediate Environment.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Safety in the Immediate Environment.

4. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Remove all guards
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   D. Run with the tool

5. When learning Introduction to Materials, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Materials.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Materials.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Materials.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Materials.

6. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Information and Communication Technology
   C. Input Cable Tester
   D. Internal Cooking Timer

7. When learning Measuring and Marking Out Tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring and Marking Out Tools.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Measuring and Marking Out Tools.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Measuring and Marking Out Tools.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Measuring and Marking Out Tools.

8. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

9. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. CPU
   B. Monitor
   C. Speaker
   D. Keyboard

10. When learning Computer Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Concepts.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Concepts.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Concepts.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Computer Concepts.

11. When learning Metallic Materials 10 3.3 Non-Metallic Materials 10 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Metallic Materials 10 3.3 Non-Metallic Materials 10 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Metallic Materials 10 3.3 Non-Metallic Materials 10 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Metallic Materials 10 3.3 Non-Metallic Materials 10 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Metallic Materials 10 3.3 Non-Metallic Materials 10 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1.

12. When learning Introduction to Drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Drawing.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Drawing.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Drawing.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Drawing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Materials and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Metallic Materials 10 3.3 Non-Metallic Materials 10 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1 and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Metallic Materials and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Non- Metallic Materials and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

1. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Pre-Technical Studies.

2. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Free-hand sketching.

3. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety in the Immediate Environment.

4. C — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

5. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Materials.

6. B — Information and Communication Technology

7. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring and Marking Out Tools.

8. D — Never touch live wires with wet hands

9. A — CPU

10. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Concepts.

11. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Metallic Materials 10 3.3 Non-Metallic Materials 10 4.0 Tools and Production 4.1.

12. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Drawing.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Introduction to Materials; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Metallic Materials; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Non- Metallic Materials; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
